scenarios.title: The Off-Season Weight
scenarios.text: You come back from the offseason heavier than the club likes, and the strength coach has a scale ready.

choices.label: Get on the scale
choices.result: You step on the scale, hear the number and spend six weeks earning back the old one.

choices.label: Bring your own numbers
choices.result: You bring your leg-speed numbers from the summer. They're better than last year, and the strength coach backs off a little.

choices.label: Laugh with the strength coach
choices.result: You joke your way through it and agree to a plan. The strength coach likes you more for it.

scenarios.title: The Captaincy
scenarios.text: The team votes for captains, and for the first time a kicker is on the ballot.

choices.label: Ask for the vote
choices.result: You tell the room why a kicker can lead too. You win by four votes.

choices.label: Let the room decide
choices.result: You don't campaign. The room votes you in anyway, and that means more.

choices.label: Take your name off
choices.result: You take your name off the ballot. A linebacker who wanted it more gets it.

scenarios.title: The Big Second Contract
scenarios.text: Your agent says this is the contract that matters, and the club agrees, eventually.

choices.label: Hold firm
choices.result: You hold firm for three tense weeks. You get your number and lose some sleep getting it.

choices.label: Take the fair deal
choices.result: You take a fair deal early and stop thinking about it. Your agent calls it smart, and means it.

choices.label: Ask the family first
choices.result: You talk it over at home before you sign. The number matters less than you thought.

scenarios.title: The Teammate Who Becomes a Coach
scenarios.text: {holder} retires and joins the coaching staff. Now they're your boss.

choices.label: Keep the friendship
choices.result: You keep the friendship and let {holder} coach you anyway. It works, mostly.

choices.label: Set new rules
choices.result: You agree on new rules: coach at the facility, friends on the weekend.

choices.label: Earn it fresh
choices.result: You treat {holder} like any new coach and earn their trust again.

scenarios.title: The Endorsement Renewal
scenarios.text: Your biggest sponsor wants to renew, with new conditions: more appearances, more posts, more of you.

choices.label: Accept the conditions
choices.result: You accept. The money is good, and your weeks get a lot shorter.

choices.label: Negotiate fewer appearances
choices.result: You negotiate the appearances down by half. They agree, grudgingly.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.result: You walk away. You get your Tuesdays back.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Charity Game
scenarios.text: You organize a charity game in your hometown with players from five clubs.

choices.label: Run it yourself
choices.result: You run every detail yourself. It's exhausting and it raises more than anyone expected.

choices.label: Bring in {best_friend}
choices.result: You put {best_friend} in charge of the day. It's the most fun either of you has had in years.

choices.label: Hire an organizer
choices.result: You hire someone who knows events. It runs perfectly, and it feels a little less like yours.

scenarios.title: The Rival Club Calls
scenarios.text: A rival club's general manager makes it clear they'd pay more, next time you're free.

choices.label: Tell your agent, nobody else
choices.result: You tell your agent and nobody else. You kick like a player who has options.

choices.label: Tell your club
choices.result: You tell your own club about the call. They appreciate it and remember it.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.result: You ignore it and kick the season out. Whatever comes, comes.

scenarios.title: The Motivation Slump
scenarios.text: Nothing's wrong. That's the problem: practice feels like a job, and the job feels like nothing.

choices.label: Take a real break
choices.result: You take your days off seriously: no film, no phone. Some of the spark comes back.

choices.label: Talk to someone
choices.result: You talk to someone about it, out loud, for the first time.

choices.label: Set a new goal
choices.result: You set a goal nobody else knows about. Practice has a point again.

scenarios.title: The Kid Who Copies Your Routine
scenarios.text: A high school kicker's video goes around: he copies your routine down to the last step.

choices.label: Send him a message
choices.result: You send him a message and a pair of cleats. His video of opening the box gets more views than yours.

choices.label: Fix one thing
choices.result: You post a short reply showing him one thing to fix. Kickers everywhere try it.

choices.label: Smile and move on
choices.result: You smile, show {love_interest} the video and move on.

scenarios.title: A Teammate Holds Out
scenarios.text: Your closest teammate is holding out for a new contract, and wants you to say something publicly.

choices.label: Back him publicly
choices.result: You back him publicly. He's grateful, and the front office notices.

choices.label: Back him privately
choices.result: You tell him you're with him and keep it out of the papers.

choices.label: Speak for the room
choices.result: You say the whole team wants him back and leave the money to the people who handle it.

scenarios.title: The Coordinator's Son
scenarios.text: The new special teams coordinator's son is a kicker on the practice squad.

choices.label: Out-kick him daily
choices.result: You out-kick him every day. It's awkward and undeniable.

choices.label: Help the kid
choices.result: You help the kid with his plant foot. The coordinator watches and says nothing, and something changes.

choices.label: Ask the coordinator directly
choices.result: You ask the coordinator directly how the job is decided. He respects the question.

scenarios.title: The Prime-Time Game
scenarios.text: Your first prime-time game in years, and the broadcast crew wants an interview at the hotel.

choices.label: Do the interview
choices.result: You do the interview and tell one good story. It runs before kickoff.

choices.label: Keep it short
choices.result: You give them ten minutes and go to bed early.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.result: You decline politely and watch film in your room.

scenarios.title: The Contract Extension
scenarios.text: The club wants to talk about extending your contract, a year early.

choices.label: Take the security
choices.result: You sign early. Your agent says you left money on the table; you sleep fine.

choices.label: Bet on yourself
choices.result: You decline and play out the deal. Every kick is an audition now.

choices.label: Ask {love_interest}
choices.result: You talk it over at home. You sign a shorter version.
